excluded_mentions.desc: The institutional 'execution alpha' model: banks/hedge funds fragment huge orders and fill them gradually around the daily/weekly VWAP and its standard-deviation bands (loading longs in the discount below VWAP, shorts in the premium above), aiming for the band extremes as optimal fill prices. Volume-driven algos like VWAP are described as best for long-duration orders (30 min to 1 day).
excluded_mentions.why_mention: Explicitly framed as NOT for the retail viewer to act on ('okay for you as a day trader with five es contracts to not care about this side of institutional trading called execution Alpha'). Presented as the background rationale for why VWAP works, not a runnable retail entry.

excluded_mentions.desc: The 'price-driven algorithms' category of institutional order-execution shown in the order-execution table, set against volume-driven algorithms such as VWAP.
excluded_mentions.why_mention: Named once as a category in the execution table but never explained or turned into a setup; no rules, levels, or runnable entry taught.

excluded_mentions.desc: ICT-style premium/discount measured off a swing high/low with the 50% midpoint of an impulse as the dividing line (below 50% = discount, above 50% = premium).
excluded_mentions.why_mention: Dispreferred / risk-contrast: presented as the arbitrary and 'very simplistic' alternative the speaker rejects in favor of VWAP's objective session-based premium/discount ('it remains an arbitrary decision where to track this'). No runnable entry is taught for it.

excluded_mentions.desc: Standard Bollinger Bands and moving averages as generic mean/volatility references.
excluded_mentions.why_mention: Dispreferred alternative cited only to argue that VWAP standard-deviation bands give 'a much deeper reason to have an edge rather than normal Ballinger bands or moving averages.' No setup is built on them.

excluded_mentions.desc: Normal volume profile as a Gaussian/bell curve with the value area (fair-value area) defined as ~70% of traded volume, i.e. one standard deviation around the average.
excluded_mentions.why_mention: Explanatory concept used to build intuition for standard deviation and 'fair value' before introducing VWAP; no runnable entry, target, or stop is taught for the volume-profile value area itself.

excluded_mentions.desc: Caveat scenario: during high momentum or an established strong trend the market keeps buying (or selling) even at premium/discount prices far from VWAP, so the reversion-to-VWAP expectation breaks down and context is required.
excluded_mentions.why_mention: Risk-contrast / caveat ('vwap is not always working it's always needed to have a context behind your trading idea'), warning when the mean-reversion fade should be avoided rather than a standalone runnable setup.
